intro.text: Someone left a note at the old school. Its clock started ringing at midnight, even though it has been silent for years.
intro.speaker: harpreet

kabirIntro.text: I hear a ticking sound. Five math locks guard a hidden time capsule. And apparently I'm the only one who brought a pencil.
kabirIntro.speaker: kabir

note.text: The chalk says: 'Round the number on the gate. Find the pattern. Count the tiles. Share the light. Measure the room.' Five locks!
note.speaker: kabir

baldev.text: I was the caretaker. We buried a time capsule long ago. The school clock only wakes up when clever young detectives arrive.
baldev.speaker: baldev

kabir.text: I'll check for secret clues while you solve the puzzles. You can always ask for a hint.
kabir.speaker: kabir

gateQuestion.text: The gate has a rounding dial. Move it to the nearest hundred, then test your answer.
gateQuestion.speaker: kabir

gateOpened.text: The gate opened! You rounded 3,472 to 3,500. That's one lock down.
gateOpened.speaker: baldev

hallwayIntro.text: Welcome to the number corridor! The floor and the wall are connected. Solve both mini-games to open the classroom.
hallwayIntro.speaker: meher

meher.text: The wall numbers keep growing in a pattern. Figure out what is being added each time.
meher.speaker: meher

rohan.text: I built these glowing tiles. Each row must have the same number of squares. Count carefully!
rohan.speaker: rohan

patternQuestion.text: The numbers on the wall are blinking. Tap the missing number to keep the pattern going.
patternQuestion.speaker: meher

patternSolved.text: Yes! 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. Each step adds six. The wall lights are on.
patternSolved.speaker: meher

arrayQuestion.text: Count the tiles in this rectangle. You can use multiplication or repeated addition.
arrayQuestion.speaker: rohan

arraySolved.text: Seven groups of eight equals fifty-six tiles! The floor is glowing like a tiny disco.
arraySolved.speaker: rohan

needHallway.text: The classroom is locked until the pattern wall AND the multiplication floor are fixed.
needHallway.speaker: meher

classroomIntro.text: This is the hidden math laboratory. Choose the correct fraction of lanterns, then measure the vault's perimeter.
classroomIntro.speaker: meena

labMeena.text: A quarter means one of four equal parts. For the vault's perimeter, count the entire distance around its edges.
labMeena.speaker: meena

labKabir.text: I found a blueprint and twelve lantern switches. They look like puzzles, not decorations.
labKabir.speaker: kabir

fractionQuestion.text: Tap the lantern switches until exactly three quarters of twelve are lit.
fractionQuestion.speaker: meena

fractionSolved.text: Nine of twelve lanterns are on. Three quarters is the same as nine twelfths. Beautiful work!
fractionSolved.speaker: meena

perimeterQuestion.text: The blueprint shows a seven-metre by five-metre rectangle. What is the total distance around it?
perimeterQuestion.speaker: harpreet

perimeterSolved.text: Twenty-four metres around! That is the perimeter. I wish our schoolwork opened real secret doors.
perimeterSolved.speaker: kabir

needLab.text: We still need both the fraction switchboard and the perimeter blueprint.
needLab.speaker: meena

vaultIntro.text: The last door just opened! That's the time capsule. Why is the clock pointing to twelve?
vaultIntro.speaker: kabir

clock.text: The hands point to twelve. Maybe the clock was saving this exact moment for us.
clock.speaker: meher

ready.text: All five locks are solved. Open the capsule and see what the old school wanted us to remember.
ready.speaker: harpreet

finalKabir.text: It's full of drawings from children who studied here years ago! One says: 'To the kids of the future—keep asking questions.'
finalKabir.speaker: kabir

finalMeher.text: Look! The missing clock hand is tucked inside the capsule with a note about friendship and curiosity.
finalMeher.speaker: meher

finalHarpreet.text: Case closed. We solved five Grade Four math puzzles, rescued a memory, and uncovered a story worth sharing.
finalHarpreet.speaker: harpreet

finalRohan.text: The clock is ticking again! And my tiles are still glowing. Can we call it an educational disco?
finalRohan.speaker: rohan

saveResume.text: Welcome back! The five math locks are still waiting for you.
saveResume.speaker: kabir

cantCombine.text: That object doesn't fit here. Explore the clues and solve each puzzle.
cantCombine.speaker: harpreet
